title: A 50 km depth-gap filter reduced the late-count depth contrast by 4.84 points at 200 km in ComCat, 2001-2024
abstract: We tested whether neighbors at different depths affect a late-count share contrast near shallow and deep earthquakes. We used a fixed USGS ComCat M5.5+ snapshot and 646 shallow and 99 deep M6.5 to below 8 centers in 2001-2024. A 50 km limit on recorded depth difference reduced the magnitude-adjusted deep-minus-shallow contrast from 21.29 to 16.45 percentage points at 200 km chord distance. The paired change was -4.84 points, with a conditional 95% three-year block interval of -11.79 to -0.59. Only four deep late pair counts were removed. A tighter 25 km filter increased the contrast by 12.27 points, and the no-isolation change interval included zero. Thus, the spatial rule affects the comparison, but it does not give a general correction or establish physical decay at depth. Sparse counts, shared events, spatial setting, depth error, selection and catalog revision limit inference. Code, annual sufficient statistics, paired draws, source hashes, external retrieval instructions, a scalar audit and a static figure are included.

display.caption: The primary 50 km depth-gap filter reduces the late-share contrast. Intervals are conditional paired three-year block intervals. Other depth limits give different results.
